# Validation: napkin estimates against real runs

<!-- Generated by `cargo run -p napkin -- validate --write VALIDATION.md` from `validation/<case>/`; edit those files instead. -->

Each case is one real job on Modal. The error ratio is observed time / predicted time, so a ratio above 1 means the real run was slower than napkin. Each tolerance was committed in `case.json` before the observation run; profile constants were not tuned to fit these cases. The runner is `modal run modal/validate.py`, an opt-in tool that is not part of CI.

| case | predicted | dominant term | observed | observed / predicted | tolerance | verdict |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| [h100-gemm-bf16](#h100-gemm-bf16) | 11 ms | compute-bound | 11 ms | 1.01 | 0.80–1.25 | within |
| [h100-pcie-roundtrip](#h100-pcie-roundtrip) | 630 ms | h2d-bound | 3.7 s | 5.90 | 0.90–1.10 | outside (slower) |
| [h100-tiny-kernels](#h100-tiny-kernels) | 17 ms | launch-bound | 62 ms | 3.64 | 0.50–2.00 | outside (slower) |

## h100-gemm-bf16: Large bf16 GEMM through cuBLAS

### Job

One bf16 GEMM C = A·B with M=16384, N=28672, K=8192 (a Llama-3-70B MLP up-projection over 16,384 tokens), bf16 inputs and output, fp32 accumulation, through torch.mm, which calls cuBLAS. Time per GEMM, back to back.

### Match

- same GPU model (NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3) and Modal request family as profiles/h100.measured.json
- same dtype (bf16 in, fp32 accumulate) and library family (cuBLAS) as the calibration
- torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_bf16_reduced_precision_reduction = False, so reductions stay fp32 as in the calibration

### Estimate inputs

- flops = 2·M·N·K = 2 × 16384 × 28672 × 8192 = 7.70 TFLOP
- hbm_bytes = 2 B × (M·K + K·N + M·N) = 2 × (134,217,728 + 234,881,024 + 469,762,048) = 1.68 GB: each operand read once and C written once, the minimum traffic
- launches = 1: one cuBLAS kernel per GEMM

```text
$ napkin estimate --gpu h100 --dtype bf16 --flops 7696581394432 --bytes 1677721600 --launches 1
H100 SXM 80GB · bf16 · measured 2026-10-12
intensity   4600 FLOP/B   ridge 230 FLOP/B   compute-bound
compute     11 ms
memory      560 μs
device      11 ms
launch      1.7 μs
total       11 ms   compute-bound
```

### Tolerance, declared before the run

0.80–1.25: The compute rate is napkin-bench's cuBLAS GemmEx bf16 on an 8192³ GEMM, the same library and dtype on a similar-sized problem, so a matched run should agree closely. The band allows two known sources of drift: the calibration's own seven GEMM samples spread from 1.36 to 1.60 ms (±8%) because sustained clocks and power vary (#5), and a different shape can select a different cuBLAS kernel and fill the 132 SMs differently (wave quantization).

### Observation

- Tool: PyTorch torch.utils.benchmark.Timer around torch.mm (cuBLAS)
- Metric: median wall time per GEMM; the Timer synchronizes CUDA before reading the clock
- Observed: 11 ms
- Timer samples: 89 samples × 10 runs per sample.
- Evidence: [case.json](validation/h100-gemm-bf16/case.json) · [run.json](validation/h100-gemm-bf16/run.json) · [timer.json](validation/h100-gemm-bf16/timer.json) · [nvidia-smi.csv](validation/h100-gemm-bf16/nvidia-smi.csv) · [timer.txt](validation/h100-gemm-bf16/timer.txt)

### Run

| field | captured value |
| --- | --- |
| captured_at | 2026-10-12T22:38:39Z |
| modal_request | H100! |
| GPU | NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 |
| driver | 610.57.04 |
| cuda_driver | 13.3 |
| torch | 2.8.0+cu129 |
| torch_cuda | 12.9 |
| cublas | 12.9.1.4 |
| PCIe peak | Gen 5 × 16 |
| SM clock | 1275–1350 MHz |
| Power | 694.73–701.14 W |
| case_seconds (GPU time) | 19.8 s |

### Result

1.01 observed / predicted — **within**.

### Excluded from the estimate

- clock and power throttling during a sustained run: the estimate uses one rate
- wave and tile quantization of this shape
- allocation and data preparation: buffers are allocated once, before timing

### Finding

Within tolerance. The run held 1275–1350 MHz SM clocks at 695–701 W, the
software power cap, which is the same sustained state the recalibrated profile
measured (#27: 691 TFLOP/s bf16 under `sw_power_cap`). cuBLAS reached
7.70 TFLOP / 11.22 ms = 686 TFLOP/s on this shape, so the 8192³ calibration
rate carried over to a 16384 × 28672 × 8192 GEMM with no visible wave or tile
quantization loss. Before #27 the profile said 734 TFLOP/s, which would have
given a ratio of about 1.07, still within the band but biased fast.

The observation host ran driver 610.57.04 while the profile was measured on
580.95.05; both are the same H100 80GB HBM3 model, so this case also shows the
GEMM rate did not move across that driver change.

## h100-pcie-roundtrip: 16 GiB host-to-device upload, then 16 GiB download

### Job

Upload 16 GiB from pinned host memory to GPU 0 as 16 queued 1 GiB copy-engine copies, then download 16 GiB back the same way: NVBandwidth host_to_device_memcpy_ce followed by device_to_host_memcpy_ce with --bufferSize 1024 --loopCount 16.

### Match

- same GPU model as profiles/h100.measured.json
- PCIe link Gen5 x16 during the copies, the link the profile was measured on; a Gen4 host halves host bandwidth and is a different system, not a miss
- pinned host memory and copy-engine copies, as in the calibration

### Estimate inputs

- h2d bytes = 16 copies × 1 GiB = 17,179,869,184 B; the same for d2h
- copy-mode async: NVBandwidth queues all 16 copies of one direction on a stream before they start, so napkin charges the fixed copy latency once per direction
- serial: the download starts after the upload finishes, so the two transfer stages add

```text
$ napkin estimate --gpu h100 --dtype fp32 --flops 0 --bytes 0 --h2d 17179869184 --h2d-copies 16 --d2h 17179869184 --d2h-copies 16 --copy-mode async
H100 SXM 80GB · fp32 · measured 2026-10-12
intensity   0 FLOP/B   ridge 17 FLOP/B   h2d-bound
compute     0 s
memory      0 s
device      0 s
h2d         ≥ 320 ms   16 async copies: 1 × 8.8 μs + 17 GB / 54 GB/s; lower bound: per-copy cost of queued async copies is unmeasured
d2h         ≥ 310 ms   16 async copies: 1 × 9.4 μs + 17 GB / 55 GB/s; lower bound: per-copy cost of queued async copies is unmeasured
total       ≥ 630 ms   h2d-bound
```

### Tolerance, declared before the run

0.90–1.10: The bandwidth constants are bulk 512 MiB pinned copies on the same kind of link, and the predicted time is almost all bytes / bandwidth (the fixed latency is 2 × 9.8 μs of about 0.6 s). NVBandwidth and napkin-bench agreed within 2% on H2D and D2H at 512 MiB (PR #25), so ±10% leaves room for host-to-host variation among PCIe Gen5 x16 Modal hosts, but not for a different link generation.

### Observation

- Tool: NVIDIA NVBandwidth v0.10.0 (commit 82fc4e8c), copy-engine memcpy testcases
- Metric: median CE bandwidth per direction over --testSamples 7, converted to time as bytes / bandwidth; observed time = upload + download
- Observed: 3.7 s
- host→device: 14.4814 GB/s → 1.186 s.
- device→host: 6.76848 GB/s → 2.538 s.
- Evidence: [case.json](validation/h100-pcie-roundtrip/case.json) · [run.json](validation/h100-pcie-roundtrip/run.json) · [nvbandwidth.json](validation/h100-pcie-roundtrip/nvbandwidth.json) · [nvidia-smi.csv](validation/h100-pcie-roundtrip/nvidia-smi.csv) · [followup.json](validation/h100-pcie-roundtrip/followup.json)

### Run

| field | captured value |
| --- | --- |
| captured_at | 2026-10-12T22:38:59Z |
| modal_request | H100! |
| GPU | NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 |
| driver | 610.57.04 |
| cuda_driver | 13.3 |
| torch | 2.8.0+cu129 |
| torch_cuda | 12.9 |
| cublas | 12.9.1.4 |
| NVBandwidth | v0.10.0 · 82fc4e8c6afa0babb8687793678f615b3b8d793e |
| PCIe peak | Gen 5 × 16 |
| SM clock | 1800–1980 MHz |
| Power | 129.24–656.36 W |
| case_seconds (GPU time) | 36.9 s |

### Result

5.90 observed / predicted — **outside (slower)**.

### Excluded from the estimate

- the host wait: NVBandwidth times copies with CUDA events while a spin kernel holds the stream, so its time excludes the issue and synchronize cost that napkin's one async latency charges (2 × 9.8 μs)
- NUMA placement: --disableAffinity is required on Modal, so host buffers are not pinned to the GPU's NUMA node
- pageable memory, which would add a staging copy
- overlap of upload and download: the job is serial by construction

### Finding

Outside tolerance, about 5.9× slower than predicted. This is a miss in the
model's assumptions, not one to tune away. The profile's 54–55 GB/s host link
is a property of the host it was measured on, not of the H100.

Confirmed from the committed evidence:

- NVBandwidth measured 14.48 GB/s upload and 6.77 GB/s download, about 27% and
  12% of the profile's bandwidth, both reported as `Passed`.
- nvidia-smi reported the link at Gen5 x16 (current and max) throughout the
  copies, so the match criterion on the link held. The link generation did not
  predict the bandwidth.
- The host ran driver 610.57.04 and nvidia-smi could not read its PCI bus id
  (`[Unknown Error]` in run.json). The profile host ran 580.95.05.
- [followup.json](validation/h100-pcie-roundtrip/followup.json): two further Modal hosts, one `H100!` (driver
  610.57.04) and one `H100!:2` (580.95.05). Both reported a Gen4 x16 link and
  ran 27.6 GB/s up and 28.5 GB/s down at both 512 MiB and 1 GiB buffers. The
  buffer size is therefore not the cause, and the same `H100!` request has
  landed on hosts with at least three different host-link bandwidths: 55, 28
  and 14/6.8 GB/s.

Hypothesis, not verified: the observation host's copy path is shared or
degraded, for example a PCIe switch contended by another tenant's GPU, or
IOMMU/virtualization overhead. Download running at half of upload is unlike
every other host measured.

Consequence for napkin: a host-copy estimate is only as good as a bandwidth
measurement from the same host. On Modal, check the host with NVBandwidth in
the same container before trusting an `h2d`/`d2h`-bound estimate.

## h100-tiny-kernels: 10,000 tiny PyTorch kernels in eager mode

### Job

A Python loop of 10,000 in-place adds on a one-element fp32 CUDA tensor (x.add_(1.0)) in PyTorch eager mode, then one synchronize: the shape of an unfused optimizer step or a small-batch decode loop.

### Match

- same GPU model as profiles/h100.measured.json
- one kernel launch per op, confirmed by the profiler's kernel count

### Estimate inputs

- flops = 10,000 adds × 1 element
- hbm_bytes = 10,000 × (4 B read + 4 B write)
- launches = 10,000: one elementwise kernel per add_ (checked with torch.profiler)

```text
$ napkin estimate --gpu h100 --dtype fp32 --flops 10000 --bytes 80000 --launches 10000
H100 SXM 80GB · fp32 · measured 2026-10-12
intensity   0.13 FLOP/B   ridge 17 FLOP/B   launch-bound
compute     0.19 ns
memory      27 ns
device      27 ns
launch      17 ms
total       17 ms   launch-bound
```

### Tolerance, declared before the run

0.50–2.00: The launch constant is napkin-bench's back-to-back empty-kernel launch through the CUDA driver API from Rust, not a framework op. The model has no term for per-op framework overhead (Python, the PyTorch dispatcher, tensor checks), so a framework loop is expected to be slower than predicted. A factor of 2 is the widest error at which a launch-bound estimate still sizes the job usefully; outside it the model is missing a term, which this case is meant to expose.

### Observation

- Tool: PyTorch torch.utils.benchmark.Timer around the loop; torch.profiler for the kernel count
- Metric: median wall time of the whole 10,000-op loop including the final synchronize
- Observed: 62 ms
- Timer samples: 9 samples × 10 runs per sample.
- Profiler counted 10000 CUDA kernels.
- Evidence: [case.json](validation/h100-tiny-kernels/case.json) · [run.json](validation/h100-tiny-kernels/run.json) · [timer.json](validation/h100-tiny-kernels/timer.json) · [nvidia-smi.csv](validation/h100-tiny-kernels/nvidia-smi.csv) · [timer.txt](validation/h100-tiny-kernels/timer.txt) · [profiler.txt](validation/h100-tiny-kernels/profiler.txt)

### Run

| field | captured value |
| --- | --- |
| captured_at | 2026-10-12T22:39:36Z |
| modal_request | H100! |
| GPU | NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 |
| driver | 610.57.04 |
| cuda_driver | 13.3 |
| torch | 2.8.0+cu129 |
| torch_cuda | 12.9 |
| cublas | 12.9.1.4 |
| PCIe peak | Gen 5 × 16 |
| SM clock | 1980–1980 MHz |
| Power | 126.73–130.17 W |
| case_seconds (GPU time) | 9.9 s |
| profiled_cuda_kernels | 10000 |

### Result

3.64 observed / predicted — **outside (slower)**.

### Excluded from the estimate

- per-op host overhead of Python and the PyTorch dispatcher
- the caching allocator: no allocations happen inside the loop
- CUDA graphs and kernel fusion, which would remove launches
- the final synchronize (about 7 μs, once)

### Finding

Outside tolerance, about 3.6× slower than predicted, as the tolerance note
anticipated. The dominant term is right: the GPU is idle most of the time.
The cost per op is wrong.

From [profiler.txt](validation/h100-tiny-kernels/profiler.txt), one profiled pass of the loop:

- 10,000 `aten::add_` calls launched exactly 10,000 kernels, and the GPU ran
  each one for 1.15 μs on average: 11.5 ms of GPU time in total.
- Each `add_` cost 7.1 μs of host time, of which `cudaLaunchKernel` took
  3.9 μs on average. The profiler adds overhead: the profiled pass took 71 ms,
  the timed passes 61.6 ms.

The unprofiled loop costs 6.16 μs per op, against napkin's 1.69 μs launch
constant. That constant is a back-to-back `cuLaunchKernel` through the driver
API from Rust (napkin-bench). It does not include the CUDA runtime wrapper, the
PyTorch dispatcher or the Python interpreter, which together cost about
4.5 μs per op on this host.

For an eager-mode framework loop, treat `--launches` × the launch constant as
a lower bound. Measure the framework's own per-op cost, about 6 μs here, before
sizing a launch-bound job. CUDA graphs or fusion remove the term, as the case
excludes.
